objectives.text: Sell the minerals on two markets at once: Chinese trade through the Chancay port, and copper into the United States under the tariff threat. Minerals are the economy; the rest follows from them. China took about a third of 2025 exports (32%, trade ministry as reported); copper to the US is under 5% of copper exports, but the US sets the tariff.

objectives.text: A stable executive after a run of removals. Congress removed Boluarte in October 2025 and José Jerí in February 2026; José María Balcázar succeeded Jerí; Keiko Fujimori was certified the winner of the 7 June runoff on 29 June 2026 after a 50,000-vote margin, and the constitutional date of office is 28 July 2026 (not confirmed in the sources read). Stability is the aim as we read the sequence.

constraints.text: Congress is the constraint. The 1993 constitution's vague 'moral incapacity' ground lets Congress remove the president, and it has done so: Castillo in December 2022, Boluarte in October 2025 and Jerí in February 2026. Each removal resets the executive's agenda, and the 2026 transition came under Balcázar, an interim president chosen by Congress.

The investment the state needs is also what brings its leaders down.

grand_strategy.reading: Peru is a minerals economy with two markets: China buys through Chancay and took about a third of 2025 exports, and the United States buys copper under a tariff set in Washington, so Lima has to keep both open at once. Its strategy is held back less by enemies than by its own Congress, which has removed three presidents since 2022 and turned the Chinese port into a political risk as well as a trade gain. Not verified for this card: the Chile, Ecuador, Bolivia, EU and Venezuela-migrant questions (no fetched source), the 1998 Ecuador accord, Bolivia's sea claim, the April 2026 first-round figures, and the Iran rupture of 1 September 2026, whose reasons the sources read do not give.

stances.note: Lima's side of the Chancay relation. The sources are mirrored from the CHN card (same URLs): the Chancay inauguration by video link on 14 Nov 2024 with Xi and Boluarte, a COSCO-owned terminal (60%, 30-year concession). Partner, not ally: no defence clause or alignment instrument was found. Warming on the volumes is our reading from the export figures (China 32% of 2025 exports, reported; not verified against the trade ministry). Friction sits under the posture: Congress removed President Jerí in February 2026 over undisclosed meetings with a Chinese businessman under scrutiny (Wikipedia pointer, tier 4). No Peruvian government statement on China was fetched; the grade is our reading of the structure (C) on top of the mirrored B evidence. Bond none: no kinship or grievance found.

stances.note: Transaction, not alignment. The United States is named by Wikipedia as Peru's number one trade partner in total trade (tier 4 pointer), and the two cooperate on counter-narcotics and under the Rio Pact. Cooling: the 2025 push on copper tariffs (Andina reported a 50% copper rate in July 2025), and the Boluarte-era rift over US condemnation of rights abuses (Wikipedia pointer). Public opinion cools too: a CFR brief links the tariffs to a sour view of the US in Peru. Peru sends under 5% of its copper to the US, so the tariff is more narrative than volume (CFR, as seen in search results). The grade is our reading (C); no source names it. Bond none: no kinship or grievance found in the sources read. Gap: the current US-Peru trade agreement status and the 2026 tariff rate are not verified.
